newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - Oct 2.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - Oct 2.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Coles Myer yesterday posted a net profit slump of 33.8 percent to A$280 million for 1995/96, a result at the lower end of senior retail analysts' expectations and confirming the market's worst fears. Due to intense competition between the major retailers, nearly all the group's nine divisions suffered what directors described as a weaker retail sector. Page 1.

As the Australian Chamber of Commerce and Industry warned yesterday the economy would be killed "stone dead" if the ACTU succeeded with its new wage claims, metal workers have negotiated a pace-setting pay deal with BTR Nylex Ltd subsidiary ACI Glass Packaging which will deliver wage increases of 16 percent over the next three years. Page 1.

Speaking with Australian Treasurer Peter Costello yesterday, United States Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan said inflation was not an immediate risk in the U.S., and he dismissed rumours that the U.S. Reserve was about to raise official rates. Costello said after the meeting that Australia's inflation was under control and would "probably" dip below the official target of two to three percent. Page 1.

The long-awaited A$475 million alliance between Ansett Australia Ltd and Air New Zealand, which will give the two airlines immediate savings of between A$50 million to A$80 million a year, took place yesterday, with promises of code sharing and seamless services linking international and domestic flights. Page 19.

In a move which is expected to be the first of many overseas investments in Australian coal, South African mining giant Ingwe Coal Corp, which produces about 60 million tonnes of steaming coal a year, yesterday took control of Coal Mines Australia Ltd in a A$230 million deal. Page 19.

After reporting a steady profit of A$238 million after tax for the year to June 30, with revenues up 4.8 percent despite a continuation of the price freeze on standard letters which has been in place since 1992, Australia Post yesterday announced plans for a A$500 million renewal of its national mail sorting centres. Page 21.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Dismissing speculation he is about to leave Coles Myer Ltd, group chief executive Peter Bartels said yesterday he does not expect any improvement in the gloomy retail outlook which contributed to Coles Myer's 28.4 percent drop in annual profit to A$302 million. Page 43.

Australia Post, the Federal Government-owned postal agency, yesterday reported a net profit of A$213.7 million for the year to June 30, 5.2 percent lower than last year, but flagged a A$500 million spending programme to develop high-technology sorting centes in Sydney and Melbourne over the next five years. Page 43.

Following weak demand from jewellery manufacturers, possible further sales from government stockpiles and suggestions by the International Monetary Fund that inflation is subdued in industrial economies, global gold prices fell to fresh lows for the year yesterday, with the gold index diving 3.1 percent on the local sharemarket. Page 43.

Optus chief operating officer Phil Jacobs revealed yesterday Optus Communications has, on the eve of its float, accelerated its network investment program with A$300 million earmarked to expand its digital mobile telephone network. Page 45.

After a last minute breakdown in discussions over a mooted fee rise and an accusation from Sky Channel managing director Bill North that Tabcorp Holdings Ltd consistently misrepresented Sky's position, pub and club broadcaster Sky last night switched off its racing service to Tabcorp's 290 agencies. Page 45.

According to an offering memorandum dated September 16 and sent to U.S. bondholders, ailing satellite pay-TV operator Australis Media Ltd has admitted it has exhausted its A$158 million interim funding facility. Australis now has just four weeks to finalise a US$150 million bond raising in the U.S. Page 45.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Coles Myer has placed the blame for a disappointing net profit slump of 34 percent to A$280.4 million for the year to July 28 on weak retailing conditions, excessive promotional spending at KMart and continuing problems in the Myer/Grace Bros department stores. Page 25.

After Australian Bureau of Statistics figures released yesterday showed total building approvals up a seasonally adjusted 1.6 percent in August, home builders are confident the worst of the housing slump is over, but still have doubts over conditions for the rest of the year. Page 25.

As applications for the A$365 million Stadium Australia float - which sees investors purchasing a gold membership to a sports club, an Olympic seat and an investment in a property trust - flow in over the coming months, the financial community will be closely examining the pricing of the deal. Page 25.

The proposed A$300 million float of the Hunter Valley coal assets of Coal Mines Australia has been scrapped following South African coal mining giant Ingwe Coal Corp making an A$85.4 million offer for the 96.3 percent share held by the AMP Society. Page 5.

Air New Zealand AIRA.NZ has finalised its A$325 million purchase of a 50 percent share in Ansett Australia. Air NZ chief executive Jim McCrea stressed that despite the transaction, both airlines would remain fiercely independent and declined to predict any shortterm fare changes. Page 27.

It has been revealed that pay-TV player Optus Vision has offered rival operator, the embattled Australis Media, up to A$13.3 million if Australis' U.S. franchisees agree to team up with Optus Vision. Optus will also offer a one-off payment of A$6.67 million for entering the proposed facility sharing joint venture. Page 27.
THE AGE

According to a Productivity Commission report into Australia's motor industry to be released today, all four of Australia's car builders and 86 percent of component manufacturers believe the government's decade old tariff reduction policy and changes to subsidies have been a good thing. Page C1.

The surge in growth by the non-bank lenders appears to be waning with Aussie Homes Loans lending volumes slumping by one-third over the past two months following aggressive marketing by the banking sector. Aussie Homes Loans lending volume has fallen from A$300 million in July to A$215 million last month. Page C1.

Despite the air of mystery surrounding Sydney's A$365 million Stadium Australia float for the 2000 Olympics and with the highly innovative nature of the floats security - a gold membership to a sports club with an Olympic seat and an investment in a propety trust - stockbrokers marketing the issue said they had received expressions of interest for most of their allocations. Page C1.

Retailing giant Coles Myer has blamed Australia's poor retailing climate, excessive spending on discount chain Kmart and ongoing problems in the Myer Grace Bros department stores for the group's 34 percent slump in net profits to A$280.4 million for the year to 28 July. Page C1.

Despite advances in communication technology, Australia Post has reported increased sales and a record profit for the past financial year. Sales grew 4.8 percent to A$2.9 billion and operating profit before tax and abnormals increased 3.8 percent to A$34.1 million. The federal government's dividend was lifted to a cool A$142.6 million. Page C3.

Shell Australia has paid an undisclosed amount for petroleum assets of Western Mining Corporation. The mining group yesterday named Shell as the new owner of its 10 percent interests in a number of oil fields on Thevenard Island off northern Western Austalia. Page C3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
